rows.title: State Spectral Gap
rows.label: thm:spectrum
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[State Spectral Gap]\label{thm:spectrum}
Fix $u\in\U$. Write $e_1=(1,0)$ and let $P_\perp(v_1,v_2)=(0,v_2)$.
The unique fixed point of the typed computable witness is
\[
 f_u^*=j(v_u^*),\qquad v_u^*=\min\{2u,1\}e_1.
\]
The map is Fr\'echet differentiable at this point exactly when $u\ne1/2$.
At these regular parameters its derivative and spectrum are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 &DT_u(f_u^*)&\sigma(DT_u(f_u^*))\\ \hline
0\le u<1/2&\tfrac12 jA&\{0,1/2\}\\[2pt]
u>1/2&\dfrac{1}{1+2u}jP_\perp A&\{0,(1+2u)^{-1}\}.
\end{array}
\]
Here the spectrum of a real operator means the spectrum of its complexification.
In both cases,
\[
 \rho(DT_u(f_u^*))=\|DT_u(f_u^*)\|
 \leq\|\widetilde K\|=\tfrac12,
 \qquad \Delta_{\mathrm{state}}:=1-\rho\geq\tfrac12.
\]
At $u=1/2$ the one-sided directional derivative is
\[
 D^+T_{1/2}(j(e_1);h)
 =\tfrac12j\bigl(Ah-e_1\max\{\langle e_1,Ah\rangle,0\}\bigr),
\]
which is not linear; a state Jacobian spectrum is not assigned there.
\end{theorem}

rows.title: Relaxation-Time Bound
rows.label: thm:relaxation
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Relaxation-Time Bound]\label{thm:relaxation}
For every fixed $u\in\U$, every $f\in\mathcal B$ and $n\geq0$,
\[
 \|T_u^n f-f_u^*\|_\infty\leq2^{-n}\|f-f_u^*\|_\infty.
\]
At a regular parameter of Theorem~\ref{thm:spectrum}, put
$\rho=\rho(DT_u(f_u^*))$. For every $r\in(\rho,1)$ there is a neighborhood
of $f_u^*$ on which the error to that fixed point decreases by a factor at
most $r$ per iteration. Every orbit eventually enters that neighborhood.
The spectral e-folding convention, in iteration units, is therefore
\[
 \tau_{\mathrm{state}}=-1/\ln\rho
 =\begin{cases}1/\ln2,&u<1/2,\\
 1/\ln(1+2u),&u>1/2,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad \frac1{\ln3}\leq\tau_{\mathrm{state}}\leq\frac1{\ln2}.
\]
The global geometric bound still holds at $u=1/2$, where this linearized
spectral convention is unavailable. It is not a physical relaxation-time
calibration or a claim that all nonlinear transients decay exactly as $\rho^n$.
\end{theorem}

rows.label: prop:weighted-history
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Finiteness, Completeness and Compactness of Weighted Histories]\label{prop:weighted-history}
The formula is finite on every pair in the full product exactly when the weighted diameters are bounded outside a finite set of stages. For finite-diameter stages this is equivalent to $B=\sup_t w_t\operatorname{diam}(S_t)<\infty$. For any nonempty inverse limit $I$ and $b\in I$, it is finite on all of $I$ exactly when $I\subseteq P_b$. If the coordinate spaces are complete and the bonding maps continuous, $P_b$ and $I\cap P_b$ are complete. If $w_t\operatorname{diam}(S_t)\to0$, the weighted metric induces the product topology and
\[
 0\leq d_w(x,y)-\max_{0\leq t\leq N} w_t d_t(x_t,y_t)
 \leq \sup_{t>N} w_t\operatorname{diam}(S_t).
\]
In this case compact coordinate spaces give a compact inverse limit. Surjective bonding maps give a compatible history through each stage point.
\end{proposition}

rows.title: Ternary Realization of E0--E2
rows.label: thm:ternary-regime-realization
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Ternary Realization of E0--E2]\label{thm:ternary-regime-realization}
Let $S_t=\{0,1\}^{t+1}$ with bonding maps that delete the last bit. Identify its inverse limit with $\mathcal I=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ and let $\mathcal E=[0,1]$. Define
\[
\phi_t(b_0,\ldots,b_t)=\sum_{j=0}^t\frac{2b_j}{3^{j+1}},
\qquad
\Phi(b)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{2b_j}{3^{j+1}}.
\]
These assignments satisfy E0, controlled E1, and E2, with
\[
a_t=\frac{2}{3^{t+2}},\qquad
A_t=\frac{1}{3^{t+1}},\qquad
\sup_b|\Phi(b)-\phi_t(p_tb)|=A_t.
\]
For distinct histories first differing at position $m$, put $d_{\mathcal I}(b,c)=3^{-(m+1)}$, and put $d_{\mathcal I}(b,b)=0$. Then
\[
d_{\mathcal I}(b,c)\leq|\Phi(b)-\Phi(c)|\leq3d_{\mathcal I}(b,c).
\]
The domain is compact and complete, and the readout is injective and bi-Lipschitz onto its image. Thus a global lower bound is realized here rather than inserted without a witness.
\end{theorem}

\]
It is attained by $g_\ast(s)=\phi_t(s)+1/(2\,3^{t+1})$.
\end{theorem}

rows.title: Joint Realization of Transport and Controlled Readouts
rows.label: thm:joint-transport-readout
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Joint Realization of Transport and Controlled Readouts]\label{thm:joint-transport-readout}
Use circle-prefix stages $S_t=\mathbb T\times\{0,1\}^t$, stage metric $\max(\rho,\mathbf{1}_{\text{different prefix}})$, and weights $w_t=3^{-t}$, where $\rho$ is circle distance with circumference one. Take the usual truncation tower $I_0$ and its variant $I_1$ with angle shift $-a$ at the single bonding level $k$, for $0<a<1/2$. Write $\beta=3^{-(k+1)}$. In the common weighted history space put $Z=I_0\cup I_1$. Let the complete codomain be $\mathcal E=\mathbb T^2\times[0,1]$ with the maximum of the first circle distance, $\beta$ times the second circle distance, and the absolute scalar difference. Define
\[
 F(x)=\left(\theta_0(x),\theta_{k+1}(x),\sum_{j\geq1}2b_j(x)3^{-j}\right).
\]
Then $d_w(x,y)\leq d_{\mathcal E}(F(x),F(y))\leq3d_w(x,y)$ on all of $Z$. On each tower the restriction satisfies E0--E2 with $a_t=2\cdot3^{-(t+1)}$ and uniform tail $A_t=3^{-t}$. The coordinate homeomorphism $H:I_0\to I_1$ shifts angles at stages $t>k$ by $a$. With projection-defect cost $E_w=3^{-k}a$, one has
\[
 d_w(x,Hx)=d_{\mathcal E}(F(x),F(Hx))=\beta a,\qquad
 d_H(I_0,I_1)=\frac{\beta a}{1+\beta}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Threshold-sensitive boundary behavior]\label{prop:threshold-sensitive-boundary}
On a fixed admissible parameter patch, suppose a candidate certificate's

and the other admissibility data remain fixed. If each margin is
$L_i$-Lipschitz, write $L=\max_iL_i$ and $m=\min_i m_i$.
A perturbation of parameter distance at most $r$ preserves a pass where
$m>Lr$ and a failure of that candidate where $m<-Lr$.
For a scalar threshold parameter with $m(\lambda_*)=0$ and
$|m(\lambda)|\geq s|\lambda-\lambda_*|$, $s>0$, measurement error $\eta$
and parameter error $r$ confine ambiguity to
\[
 |\lambda-\lambda_*|\leq(\eta+Lr)/s.
\]
Thus a band-width bound requires an explicit transversal lower slope;
no universal narrow band follows without it.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Realized Contractive Bridge with Nonconstant Equilibria]\label{thm:realized-nonconstant-bridge}
Let $0<\kappa<1$, let $\U$ be a nonempty compact interval, and let a nonconstant Lipschitz profile $a:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfy
\[
0\leq a(s)+u\leq1-\kappa\qquad(s\in[0,1],\ u\in\U).
\]
Take ${C_{\mathrm{proj}}}=C$, $Kf=\kappa\int_0^1f$, and $\Gamma(u)(s)=a(s)+u$. Let $a_{N,i}=N\int_{I_{N,i}}a$ and
\[
\widehat T_{N,u}(\mathbf{x})_i
=\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}\left(\kappa\frac1N\sum_jx_j+a_{N,i}+u\right).
\]
This finite transition has the original increment form: choose all $N$ nodes as incoming neighbors (including self-edges), $I_j(x_j)=x_j$, $e_i=\phi_i=0$, $k=T=1$, $\theta=N/\kappa$, $\eta=\alpha=\beta=1$, $D=0$, $B(\mathbf{x})=-\mathbf{x}$ and $\Gamma_{N,i}=a_{N,i}+u$. The assumptions of the discrete contraction and bridge theorems hold with $\rho_N=\kappa$ and
\[
\eps_N=\norm{P_Na-a}\leq\frac{L_a}{\sqrt{12}\,N}.
\]
Writing $\bar a=\int_0^1a$, the equilibria are
\[
f_u^\ast(s)=a(s)+u+\kappa\frac{\bar a+u}{1-\kappa},\qquad
\widehat f_{N,u,i}^\ast=a_{N,i}+u+\kappa\frac{\bar a+u}{1-\kappa}.
\]

\[
\norm{J_N\widehat f_{N,u}^\ast-f_u^\ast}
=\norm{P_Na-a}\leq\frac{L_a}{\sqrt{12}\,N},\qquad

\]

\begin{proposition}[Fibre Truncation Has a Sharp Commutation Defect]\label{prop:sigma-fibre-truncation}
On the tower $(p,\theta,b)$ with $c(b)=\sum_{j\ge1}2b_j3^{-j}$, fix $m\ge1$ and let $b^\star=(0,1,0,1,\ldots)$. The truncation $T_m$ fixes $p,\theta,b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and fills the tail with that of $b^\star$. For $\Phi_{u,q}(p,\theta,b)=(p,u+q\lambda b_1,Rb)$ with $Rb=(0,1-b_1,1-b_2,\ldots)$, its pointwise commutation defect is
\[
 d(T_m\Phi_{u,q}x,\Phi_{u,q}T_m x)
 =2\,3^{-(m+1)}\,\mathbf1_{b_m\ne b^\star_m}.
\]
In particular the uniform defect is exactly $2\,3^{-(m+1)}$.
\end{proposition}

rows.title: Fixed-Point Displacement under Approximate Commutation
rows.label: thm:sigma-approximate-displacement
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Fixed-Point Displacement under Approximate Commutation]\label{thm:sigma-approximate-displacement}
Let $\Sigma$ be an $L$-Lipschitz self-map of a nonempty complete metric space, where $0\le L<1$, and let $p$ be its fixed point. For each intervention self-map $\Phi_u$ define
\[
 e_u(p)=d(\Sigma\Phi_u(p),\Phi_u\Sigma(p)),\qquad
 \varepsilon_u=\sup_x d(\Sigma\Phi_u(x),\Phi_u\Sigma(x)).
\]
Then $d(\Phi_u(p),p)\le e_u(p)/(1-L)\le\varepsilon_u/(1-L)$. In particular,
\[
 (1-L)d(\Phi_u(p),\Phi_v(p))\le e_u(p)+e_v(p).
\]
If both uniform defects are bounded by $\varepsilon$, the separation is at most $2\varepsilon/(1-L)$. Both bounds are sharp, including simultaneously on rational affine models.
\end{theorem}

rows.title: Independent-Block Risk and Coverage Inference
rows.label: thm:independent-block-risk-intervals
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Independent-Block Risk and Coverage Inference]\label{thm:independent-block-risk-intervals}
Let $M$ count covered decisions and $K$ count wrong covered decisions among $n$ independent blocks. Then
\[
 M\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,C),\qquad K\mid M\sim\operatorname{Bin}(M,e),
 \qquad e=\Pr(W=1\mid B=1)\quad(C>0).
\]
With $I_C=I_{\alpha_C}(M,n)$ and $I_e=I_{\alpha_e}(K,M)$, simultaneous coverage is at least $1-\alpha_C-\alpha_e$. When $M=0$ retain $I_e=[0,1]$ and leave sample conditional error unreported. The minimum and maximum of $\gamma(1-c)+cx$ over the corners of $I_C\times I_e$ give risk bounds simultaneous with $I_C$.

A direct joint alternative uses counts $N=(K,M-K,n-M)$ and probabilities $\theta=(Ce,C(1-e),1-C)$. Let $f_\theta$ be their multinomial mass and define
\[
 p_\theta(N)=\sum_{\substack{m_1+m_2+m_3=n\\f_\theta(m)\le f_\theta(N)}} f_\theta(m),
 \qquad \mathcal Q_\alpha(N)=\{\theta:p_\theta(N)>\alpha\}.
\]
Projecting $\mathcal Q_\alpha$ onto $C=\theta_1+\theta_2$ and $R_\gamma=\theta_1+\gamma\theta_3$, using infima and suprema, yields a simultaneous exact confidence region with coverage at least $1-\alpha$.

Suppose a justified leak cap is $p_U$. For a stochastic audit, let an audit flag $D$ satisfy $\mathbf1_E\le D$ almost surely in the same target population. From $J$ flags in $n_D$ independent audit blocks, the upper endpoint of $I_{\alpha_D}(J,n_D)$ can supply $p_U$. With simultaneous coverage endpoints $C_L,C_U$ and risk upper endpoint $R_U$, certify the preregistered minimum coverage and a fixed positive margin $\eta$ against the applicable null floor only if
\[
 C_L\ge C_{\min},\qquad R_U\le B_\star(C_U,p_U)-\eta .
\]
Under that null this certification has probability at most $\alpha_C+\alpha_e+\alpha_D$ for the rectangle construction, or $\alpha+\alpha_D$ for the joint construction. A deterministic certified cap uses $\alpha_D=0$.
\end{theorem}

\[

\begin{proposition}[Noise-robust null exclusion]\label{prop:noise-margin}\leavevmode\par
Let $e_i=\Phi(z_i)$ and estimates $\widehat e_i$ satisfy $\dE(e_i,\widehat e_i)\leq\eta_i$, $i=0,1$. Let $m=C\epsilon$ be a certified true separation. Then

\[
m>\eta_0+\eta_1+r_0+r_1.
\]
For equal estimation and acceptance radii $\eta$, this sufficient condition is $m>4\eta$, not merely $m>2\eta$.
\end{proposition}

rows.title: Exact Independent-Block Win Test and Power
rows.label: thm:campaign-block-sign-test
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact Independent-Block Win Test and Power]\label{thm:campaign-block-sign-test}
Suppose $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ are independent Bernoulli variables and $\Pr(W_i=1)\le1/2$ under the sign null. For a fixed $k$, the rejection probability of $\sum_i W_i\ge k$ is at most
\[
 B_{n,k}(1/2)=2^{-n}\sum_{j=k}^n {n\choose j}.
\]
For iid success probability $\pi$ the power is exactly $B_{n,k}(\pi)=\sum_{j=k}^n{n\choose j}\pi^j(1-\pi)^{n-j}$. With $n=20$, $\alpha=1/20$ and $k=15$, the size is at most $5425/262144<\alpha$ and the power at $\pi=4/5$ exceeds $4/5$. The threshold $14$ fails the size requirement.
\end{theorem}

rows.title: A Calibrated Blockwise Falsation Bound
rows.label: thm:external-interface-falsation-bound
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[A Calibrated Blockwise Falsation Bound]\label{thm:external-interface-falsation-bound}
For a frozen family of $m\ge1$ directional contrasts, let independent block vectors have scores $D_{ik}\in[-1,1]$. Independence between coordinates $k$ is not required. Suppose $\mu_k=n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb E D_{ik}\ge\eta_k$ is a prediction of the declared realized model; identically distributed blocks are not required. Assume uniform readout calibration error at most $e$ on an event of probability at least $1-\beta$, $0\le\beta\le1$, and score Lipschitz constant $L$ for each arm, so the recorded contrast differs from its ideal score by at most $2Le$. Let $0<\alpha<1$ and
\[
 t_n=\sqrt{\frac{2\log(m/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]
The rule rejecting the joint directional prediction when some recorded mean is below $\eta_k-t_n-2Le$ has false rejection probability at most $\min(1,\alpha+\beta)$. If the actual decision can be coupled to this specified blind design so that it agrees outside a failure event of probability at most $p$, the bound is at most $\min(1,\alpha+\beta+p)$. An audit pass fraction alone does not establish that coupling.

For an alternative with some fixed $\mu_k\le\eta_k-g$, let $0<\zeta<1$ and $t_\zeta=\sqrt{2\log(1/\zeta)/n}$. If $g>t_n+t_\zeta+4Le$, rejection probability is at least $\max(0,1-\zeta-\beta-p)$ under the same coupling. For $g>4Le$, it suffices that
\[
 n>\frac{\bigl(\sqrt{2\log(m/\alpha)}+\sqrt{2\log(1/\zeta)}\bigr)^2}{(g-4Le)^2}.
\]
These are design-conditional guarantees, not a universal biological sample size.
\end{theorem}

rows.title: Sharp Single-Readout Resolution of Tower Identity
rows.label: thm:tower-identity-observation-resolution
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Sharp Single-Readout Resolution of Tower Identity]\label{thm:tower-identity-observation-resolution}
In the common history metric and the common readout metric, respectively,
\[
 d_H(I_a,I_{a'})=d_H(F(I_a),F(I_{a'}))
 =\frac{\beta}{1+\beta}\rho(a,a').
\]
Here $F$ is the same early-phase, late-phase and ternary readout applied to every branch in the comparison. Two specified alternatives can be distinguished uniformly from a single observation with error at most $\eta$ if and only if
\[
 \rho(a,a')>2(1+\beta^{-1})\eta.
\]
A decoder can use the measured phase difference $z=y_1-y_0$ and retain every alternative within circle distance $(1+\beta^{-1})\eta$ of $z$. For a separated family it returns the unique compatible alternative. A continuous interval of jumps has zero uniform deformation gap over distinct alternatives.
\end{theorem}

rows.title: Identity Separation from an Addressable Control Interface
rows.label: thm:addressable-identity-alternatives
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Identity Separation from an Addressable Control Interface]\label{thm:addressable-identity-alternatives}
For two candidate profiles $p,p'$ write $d_t=p_t-p'_t$. Their branch sets have exact Hausdorff distance, both in the common history space and in the calibrated readout space,
\[
 D(p,p')=\max_{0\le i,j\le K+1}
 \frac{w_iw_j}{w_i+w_j}|d_i-d_j|.
\]
The family of distinct candidates has minimum separation
\[
 g=\frac{1}{M(3^{K+1}+1)}.
\]
Uniform identification from one observation with unknown initial phase and adversarial error at most $\eta$ is possible for the entire family exactly when $2\eta<g$. The measurement can return the set of compatible profiles and give a unique label only when that set is a singleton. Allowing continuous amplitudes or unbounded jump addresses removes the uniform gap. Omitting intermediate phase observations can make different addresses with the same amplitude identical to the observer.
\end{theorem}

rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Legibility of Matched Integration Responses]\label{thm:matched-integration-legibility}
Use the windows of Definition~\ref{def:matched-paired-response-window} with $\lambda\in\{0\}\cup[L,1/9]$ and adversarial observation error at most $\eta=1/256$ in the paired metric. The following are the L1--L6 properties of Definition~\ref{def:ileg} evaluated on the paired-response domain.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item The clean high and low response sets have separation exactly $L$.
\item All observations in the allowed noise balls preserve the clean class, with zero abstentions.
\item For any train of at least three freshly reset pairs at a fixed coupling and fixed prepared first bit, the class persists when the common input phase varies across pairs.
\item In the nonempty target population, retain the same state and common input, prepare $b_1=1$, and ablate $\lambda\in[L,1/9]$ to zero between paired trials. The class changes from high to low with zero misses.
\item In the nonempty sham population, retain the state and coupling and vary the common input across paired trials. Both first-bit strata are allowed. The false-change and abstention rates are zero.
\item On the resolved domain one bit retains the class with zero discrete class distortion, and zero bits are insufficient. Including the audit status of abstention requires two bits in a fixed-length encoding.
\end{enumerate}
At error radius $L/2$ a low and a high experiment can have identical full observations. If the common-input condition is removed, even a noise-free uncoupled experiment can decode as high.
\end{theorem}

For exact structural equivalence on the complete domains required by the six predicates,
\[
 S_1\in\Cop\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S_2\in\Cop.
\]
The induced map is
\[
 \widehat\chi:\Qop(S_1)\longrightarrow\Qop(S_2),\quad [x]\mapsto[\chi x],
\]
with $\widehat\chi$ a bijection. Invariant or partition preservation is not an additional hypothesis.
\end{theorem}

rows.title: Conditional Use of Single-Rupture Schemas
rows.label: thm:six-witness-schemas
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Conditional Use of Single-Rupture Schemas]\label{thm:six-witness-schemas}
Consider these six candidate schemas. A schema separates its target invariant
from the other five only when an admissible model realizes the five retained
predicates and fails the target on the same declared comparison domain:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{Persistence witness.} A system with a certified decoder,
non-factorizable causal structure, unique identity label, continuous class map,
and non-null differentiation, but whose admissible support exits the declared
forward-invariant domain under some $u\in U$.
\item \textbf{Rigid-identity witness.} A system with persistent support,
integration, continuity, differentiation, and legibility, but with two
compatible non-isomorphic identity candidates transported by the same readout
family.
\item \textbf{Integration witness.} A product system
$A_S=A_1\times A_2$ with persistent factors, unique factor identities,
continuous dynamics, non-null differentiation, and certified decoders, but with
decoupled intervention histories so that the aggregate factorizes.
\item \textbf{Continuity witness.} A system with persistent support, unique
identity, non-factorizable structure, non-null differentiation, and certified
decoders, but with an admissible transition producing a jump between
incompatible regime classes.
\item \textbf{Differentiation witness.} A persistent, rigid, integrated,
continuous, and legible system whose decoder-visible classes collapse to a
stable null or single indistinguishable class.
\item \textbf{Legibility witness.} A persistent, rigid, integrated, continuous,
and non-null differentiated system whose class partition is latent but no
certified decoder satisfies L1--L6.
\end{enumerate}
Existence of the six models is a separate obligation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sufficiency of the six-invariant basis]\label{thm:six-sufficiency}
Let $S$ be admissible on support $\Aset$. If
\[
\Iper(S)=\Iri(S)=\Iint(S)=\Icont(S)=\Idiff(S)=\Ileg(S)=1,
\]
then $S$ satisfies every structural burden required for membership in $\Cop$ as
defined in this paper. No additional independent predicate can invalidate
$S\in\Cop$ without changing the definition of $\Cop$ or causing at least one of
the six invariants to fail.
\end{theorem}

rows.label: thm:infinite-strict-upstream-separation
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Infinite-Dimensional Strict Upstream Separation]\label{thm:infinite-strict-upstream-separation}
Fix the global Hilbert--prefix feedback system and comparison data of Paper V, together with the following preregistered valuation protocol. Exchange the two Hilbert coordinate groups by $P(z^L,z^R)=(z^R,z^L)$, leaving the phase and bit variables unchanged. Prepare a $P$-invariant state, use paired controls $v$ and $Pv$ at equal cost, and transport the reference and measurement coordinates by the same exchange. For the weighted response take any nonnegative, bounded, $P$-invariant functional of deviation from the sham reference on a finite horizon, for example the sum of squared Hilbert deviations and squared phase distances. Use the same population law for a control and its paired image and a positive valuation scale $s_V$.

This system satisfies all six global upstream predicates and has $\widehat{\ValAsym}_\tau=0$ for every such admissible horizon. Consequently it is not in $\Subfp(\tau)$ at any positive gate threshold. In the common universe of systems equipped with these typed comparison/measurement data, restricted to infinite-dimensional supports,
\[
 \Subfp(\tau)\subsetneq\Cop.
\]
Here the model universe consists of fully specified systems, including their declared admissibility, decoder/comparator and measurement data, as required by Definition~\ref{def:subfp}. For the infinite-support subuniverse $\mathfrak M_\infty$, the precise restricted statement is $(\Subfp(\tau)\cap\mathfrak M_\infty)\subsetneq(\Cop\cap\mathfrak M_\infty)$. The same witness also makes the unrestricted upstream inclusion proper. $\Subfp$ is the historical first-person class alias for the seven-coordinate indexed certificate class. The conclusion is about the formal classes, not about experiential properties, and does not assert nonemptiness of the stronger class. It does not quantify over every possible differently instrumented extension of an unspecified bare plant.
\end{theorem}

rows.title: Exact Separation by an Accessible Private Signal
rows.label: thm:writable-tower-private-return-separation
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact Separation by an Accessible Private Signal]\label{thm:writable-tower-private-return-separation}
Retain the hidden return task of Theorem~\ref{thm:writable-tower-public-return-tie}. Let the candidate alone receive a finite signal $Z$ at decision time, with laws $\mu_x^+$ and $\mu_x^-$ conditional on the public stratum $x$ and the successful action signs $+1$ and $-1$, respectively. Assume the signal is available in one permitted reading and the decision maps used for the stated optima can be fixed from the declared signal law within the budget, without fitting on the reserve. For the worst-sign optimum this includes the allowed randomization from a fixed map of the reading to an action probability. The predictor retains only its sampled binary decision. For stratum weights $w_x$, the exact best signed margin against the public rival closure is
\[
 \sup_{\text{candidate}}\inf_{\text{public rival}}(R_{\mathrm{rival}}-R_{\mathrm{candidate}})
 = \frac12 \sum_x w_x\,\operatorname{TV}(\mu_x^+,\mu_x^-),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{TV}(\mu,\nu)=\frac12\sum_z|\mu(z)-\nu(z)|.
\]
It is positive exactly when the two accessible laws differ on a positive-weight stratum.

Under minimax over the two successful action signs at fixed $x$, allowing randomization, the best private risk is
\[
 \max_{0\le\pi\le1}\sum_z
       \min\{\pi\mu_x^+(z),(1-\pi)\mu_x^-(z)\}.
\]
It is strictly below the public minimax risk $1/2$ exactly when $\mu_x^+\ne\mu_x^-$. For a uniform worst-sign improvement across the finitely many strata, each pair of accessible laws must differ and their respective optimal rules must be jointly admissible. If the same signal and decision budget are shared with the rivals, their closure can reproduce the candidate decision and the best signed margin is zero.
\end{theorem}

rows.label: prop:base-wedge-metric-sector

\begin{proposition}[Metric-Sector Stability of the Hilbert Wedge]
\label{prop:base-wedge-metric-sector}
For $Q=\{0\le z_j\le2^{-j}\}\subset\ell^2$ let
$W=(Q\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times Q)$ and $R=1/\sqrt3$.
Cartesian products in these fixed axes, with both factor diameters at least
$d_0>0$, have Hausdorff distance at least $\max\{d_0/2,R/2\}$ from W.
More generally, for maximum-metric products of compact factors with these
diameter bounds and embeddings with uniform constants $0<c\le C$,
\[
 d_H(W,F(A\times B))\ge
 \delta_W:=\frac{c^2\min\{d_0/2,1/(4C)\}}{2C+4c}>0.
\]
Every nonempty compact support at distance less than $\delta_W/2$ from W
therefore retains a gap greater than $\delta_W/2$ against this same sector.
\end{proposition}

rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Bounded-Distortion Wedge Gap]\label{thm:wedge-bilipschitz-gap}
Let A and B be nonempty compact metric spaces of diameter at least $d_0>0$.
Give $A\times B$ the maximum metric. Suppose an embedding
$F:A\times B\to H\oplus H$ satisfies
\[
 c\,d_\infty(p,p')\le\|F(p)-F(p')\|\le C\,d_\infty(p,p'),
 \qquad 0<c\le C.
\]
Put
\[
 d_*:=\min\{d_0/2,1/(4C)\},\qquad
 \delta_W:=\frac{c^2d_*}{2C+4c}.
\]
Then $d_H(W,F(A\times B))\ge\delta_W>0$. Consequently, if a nonempty compact
$\widetilde W$ satisfies $d_H(W,\widetilde W)<r_W:=\delta_W/2$, its distance
from every product in this same $(d_0,c,C)$ sector exceeds $\delta_W/2$.
The factors need not be assumed path connected.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Operational Barrier and Cheap-Damage Contrast]
\label{prop:wedge-energy-regimes}
On W let $D_{s_L,s_R}(x,y)=((1-s_L)x,(1-s_R)y)$,
$s_L,s_R\in[0,1]$, and $s=\max\{s_L,s_R\}$. These maps commute with all

\[
 M_{\rm damage}=0,\qquad
 M_{\rm protected}=R+R^{-1}=4/\sqrt3>2/3.
\]
The actual damage clamp $D_{0,1}$ has cost $K_{\rm atom}=1/3$ and
deformation $R\ge\delta_{\rm atom}=1/2$, so it enforces
$M_{\rm damage}\le K_{\rm atom}/\delta_{\rm atom}=2/3$.
The protected sector admits that clamp only at cost $4/3>K_{\rm atom}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Exact Loss Against the Entire Causal Closure]
\label{lem:indexed-causal-closure-loss}
On the balanced sign cube, let $\chi=\sigma xy$. The native controller applies
to Hilbert coordinate j the inputs
\[
 v_j^L=(a_jxy/4)(1+g\sigma),\qquad
 v_j^R=(a_jxy/4)(1-g\sigma),
\]
with $q=u=0$, initial $z=\bar z$, and $\theta=0$. Its normalized physical
contrast at the next step is
\[
 T_g=\frac8{a_j}\bigl[(z_j^{L\prime}-\bar z_j^L)
                         -(z_j^{R\prime}-\bar z_j^R)\bigr]=g\chi.
\]

rows.label: thm:readout-loss-stability
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Quantitative Stability of Audited Readout Loss]\label{thm:readout-loss-stability}
Let $Z$ be a compact metric space, $X\subseteq Z$ a nonempty compact set,
$\Theta$ a nonempty compact control space, and $h:\Theta\times X\to Z$
continuous. Let $F:Z\to\mathcal E$ be continuous into a metric space.
For $r\geq0$ define its uniform modulus and the comparison quantities
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \omega_F(r)&=\sup_{d_Z(z,z')\leq r}d_{\mathcal E}(Fz,Fz'),\\
 \Delta&=\max_{\theta\in\Theta,\,x\in X}d_Z(x,h_\theta x),\\
 R(F,h)&=\max_{\theta,x}d_{\mathcal E}(Fx,F(h_\theta x)),\qquad
 P(F,h)=\frac{r_0}{r_0+R(F,h)},\quad r_0>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
These maxima are finite, and $\omega_F(r)\to0$ as $r\downarrow0$. If a
lower bound $d_{\mathcal E}(Fx,F(h_\theta x))\geq C d_Z(x,h_\theta x)$
holds on these compared pairs, then
\[
 C\Delta\leq R(F,h)\leq\omega_F(\Delta).
\]
For another readout $G:Z\to\mathcal E$ and transport family $h'$ on the same
domains, suppose, with $\eta,\zeta\geq0$,
\[
 \sup_{z\in Z}d_{\mathcal E}(Fz,Gz)\leq\eta,
 \qquad \sup_{\theta,x}d_Z(h_\theta x,h'_\theta x)\leq\zeta.
\]
Using a supremum for $R(G,h')$ if a maximum is not attained, one has
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |R(F,h)-R(G,h')|&\leq2\eta+\omega_F(\zeta),\\
 |P(F,h)-P(G,h')|&\leq\frac{2\eta+\omega_F(\zeta)}{r_0}.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular $R(F,h)\geq C\delta$ for any witnessed displacement
$d_Z(x,h_\theta x)\geq\delta>0$. Such positivity survives a comparison
error smaller than $C\delta$. No scalar mass label supplies the common
domain, lower bound, transport or uniform approximation hypotheses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Nontrivial Energy--Phase Coupled Bridge]\label{prop:coupled-energy-phase-bridge}
Let $\nu=kT>0$, with energy coordinates and $\nu$ expressed in the same normalized energy unit and phases in radians. Fix Lipschitz profiles $e:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ and a real lift
$\phi:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ with constants $L_e,L_\phi$ such that
\[
 |e(s)-e(t)|\leq E_0,\qquad
 |\phi(s)-\phi(t)|\leq\theta_0<\pi/2.
\]
Define the positive kernel and operator
\[
 w(s,t)=\frac{\exp(-|e(s)-e(t)|/\nu)}{\cos(\phi(s)-\phi(t))},
 \qquad (K_wf)(s)=\kappa\int_0^1w(s,t)f(t)\,dt.
\]
Assume $0<\kappa$, $q:=\kappa\sec\theta_0<1$, and let a nonconstant
$L_a$-Lipschitz profile $a$ and a nonempty compact control interval $\U$ satisfy
$0\leq a(s)+u\leq1-q$. Set $T^w_u=P_C(K_w\cdot+a+u)$.
For $s_i=(i-1/2)/N$, freeze $e_i=e(s_i)$, $\phi_i=\phi(s_i)$ and set
\[
 (\widehat T^w_{N,u}\mathbf x)_i
 =\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}
 \left(\frac\kappa N\sum_{j=1}^Nw(s_i,s_j)x_j+a_{N,i}+u\right).
\]
This is the original increment operator with the complete directed graph
(self-edges included), $I_j=\operatorname{Id}$, $\theta=N/\kappa$,
$\eta=\alpha=\beta=1$, $B=-\operatorname{Id}$ and $D=0$.

Both maps are $q$-contractive in their Hilbert norms. More generally the
same phase sector gives the sufficient directed-graph factor
\[
 q_N=|1-\alpha\beta|
 +\frac{\eta L_I\sqrt{d_N^{\rm in}d_N^{\rm out}}}{\theta\cos\theta_0}
 +\alpha L_D<1.
\]
With $P_N=J_NJ_N^\dagger$ and
\[
 L_w=\sec\theta_0\left(\frac{L_e}{\nu}+\tan\theta_0 L_\phi\right),
 \qquad \varepsilon_N=\frac{\kappa L_w+L_a/\sqrt{12}}{N},
\]
the coupled discretization satisfies
\[
 \sup_{f\in C}\|J_N\widehat T^w_{N,u}J_N^\dagger f-T^w_uf\|_2
 \leq\varepsilon_N,
 \qquad
 \|J_Nx^*_{N,u}-f^*_{w,u}\|_2\leq\frac{\varepsilon_N}{1-q}.
\]
In particular the requested one-step comparison holds for $f=J_N\mathbf x$.
Let $d_0=\|a-\bar a\|_2$, $d_{0,N}=\|P_Na-\bar a\|_2$ and
\[
 b_w=\max\{1-e^{-E_0/\nu},\sec\theta_0-1\},
 \qquad b_*:=\frac{\kappa b_w}{1-q}.
\]
Then, uniformly in $u$,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(f^*_{w,u},\mathcal N)\geq d_0-b_* ,\qquad
 \operatorname{dist}_N(x^*_{N,u},\mathcal N_N)\geq d_{0,N}-b_* .
\]
Whenever the respective right side is positive, non-collapse follows without
assuming H5. Here $\mathcal N_N$ is the space of constant vectors.

A genuinely coupled, uniformly nonempty sector is
\[
 \nu=1,\quad\kappa=1/4,\quad a(s)=s/4,\quad\U=[0,1/4],
 \quad e(s)=\phi(s)=s/64.
\]
For this choice $q\leq2048/8191$ and both gaps, for every $N\geq2$, are at least
\[
 \gamma:=\frac1{16}-\frac{8191}{256\cdot6143}
          =\frac{90097}{1572608}>0.
\]
Energy and phase vary between nodes and across the declared parameter sector;
they remain fixed during each coherence iteration. No evolution law or
contractivity for a joint time-varying energy--phase state is asserted.
\end{proposition}

rows.title: Countable Metric--Polish Consistency
rows.label: thm:compact-polish-consistency
rows.source_statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Countable Metric--Polish Consistency]\label{thm:compact-polish-consistency}
Let $(S_n,d_n)_{n\geq0}$ be nonempty complete separable metric spaces with
continuous bonding maps. Put $b_n=\min\{1,d_n\}$ and choose $w_n>0$ with
$\sum_nw_n<\infty$. On the full coordinate product define
\[
 \bar d_w(x,y)=\sup_n w_n b_n(x_n,y_n).
\]
This is a finite complete separable metric inducing exactly the product
topology. The inverse limit is closed, hence is Polish whenever nonempty.
If the stages are compact metric, the inverse limit is compact metric and
nonempty, even without surjectivity of the bonding maps. Surjectivity also
makes every canonical projection onto its stage surjective.

For the normalized metrics already declared above, $b_n=d_n$ and
$\bar d_w=\dw$. For unnormalized compact coordinate metrics, the raw formula
$\sup_n w_nd_n(x_n,y_n)$ has the same topology and compactness conclusions
under the explicit tail condition $w_n\operatorname{diam}(S_n)\to0$.
Summability of weights alone is not that condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Compatible Observable Channels and Detectability]\label{thm:channel-projection-detectability}
Let two countable towers have chosen coordinate metrics $d_n,e_n$, weights
$w_n,v_n>0$, and finite weighted supremum metrics inducing their product
topologies, for example those of Theorem~\ref{thm:compact-polish-consistency}.

$q_n:Y_{n+1}\to Y_n$. A declared observable-channel realization supplies maps
$C_n:S_n\to Y_n$ satisfying the exact law
\[
 q_n C_{n+1}=C_n\pi_n\qquad(n\geq0).
\]
Then $C_\infty(x)_n=C_n(x_n)$ is a map between their inverse limits and
$p_n^Y C_\infty=C_np_n^S$. It is continuous if every $C_n$ is continuous.
If $c_n>0$ and
\[
 e_n(C_na,C_nb)\geq c_nd_n(a,b),\qquad
 C_0:=\inf_n\frac{v_nc_n}{w_n}>0,
\]
then $d_Y(C_\infty x,C_\infty y)\geq C_0d_S(x,y)$.
For a post-readout $L:\mathcal I_Y\to\E$ with lower constant $\ell>0$
on the compared image pairs, $\Phi=L\circ C_\infty$ has lower constant
$C=\ell C_0$ on the corresponding pairs. A single certified stage comparison
$d_n(x_n,y_n)\geq\epsilon_n>0$ also gives the pair bound
\[
 \dE(\Phi(x),\Phi(y))\geq\ell v_nc_n\epsilon_n.
\]

conditions on the coordinate maps of a channel, not an identification of a
channel object with a map or a derivation of its calibration from CCR.
